args.query: statement timeout shared database slow query seq scan autovacuum

events.statement: order-service is not the only ledger-db consumer: ledger-db is a shared postgres used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
order-service errors begin at 09:00:42 and are almost entirely ledger-db statement timeouts on INSERT INTO orders (284 ERROR entries).
order-service p99 latency jumps from ~150ms (stable through the 08:30 bucket) to a 08:45-bucket avg of 512ms (max 5607ms) and then a sustained ~5200-5300ms from 09:00 onward.
order-service db_pool_in_use rises from ~14 to ~46 connections at the same 08:45-09:00 window, consistent with connections blocked on the DB.
portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905) was deployed at 08:56:00Z with a change 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at' and 'no migration included'; it is still live (not rolled back).
ledger-db logs show this exact new portfolio-service query doing a Seq Scan on a 48,211,907-row trades table, taking 1-9 seconds per call; first occurrence 08:58:38Z.
ledger-db CPU jumps from ~30% (flat through 08:30) to a 08:45-bucket max of 96.36% and a sustained ~96% from 09:00.
ledger-db slow_queries_per_min jumps from ~1/min (through 08:30) to a 08:45-bucket max of 139.68 and a sustained ~140/min from 09:00.
ledger-db connections_active rises from ~62 to a 08:45-bucket max of 199.81 and a sustained ~190 from 09:00.
The only config change in the window is cfg-2903: ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1 at 08:00:00Z.
Other ledger-db consumers are essentially unaffected: payment-service produced 0 WARN+ entries and settlement-service only 1 connection-reset warning in the incident window.

A past incident HIST-111 with the same shape (a new report query without an index doing full table scans on ledger-db, high DB CPU) was classified bad_deployment and resolved by adding an index plus a query review gate.
